title: Moving House
description: Ten short stories about moving to a new home: finding a place, moving day, a new town, an old house, a hard first week, a garage sale, a small repair, a street fair, a new life in a big city and a first winter.

lessons.title: A Home for Two
lessons.summary: Anna and David, who are newly married, find a place of their own with the help of an agent.
lessons.text:
Anna and David got married in June. Since then, they have lived with David's parents. The house is small, so now Anna and David want a home of their own.

Anna and David both work long hours, so they decided to use an agent. An agent helps people find a home. Their agent was a woman named Karen. At their first meeting, Karen asked them a lot of questions.

"Is there a particular part of the city that you like?" Karen asked.

"Yes," Anna said. "The location is very important to us. We both work in the center of the city, so we want a location near the train."

"Do you need anything else in particular?" Karen asked.

"We have a dog," David said. "His name is Max. Are dogs allowed in most buildings?"

"Some owners allow dogs, and some don't," Karen said. "We will only look at places where dogs are allowed."

Then Karen explained the rules. "Most owners ask for 2 things. First, papers that show your income are required. Your income has to be about 3 times the cost of the place each month. Second, a reference is required. Usually, a reference is a letter from the owner of your previous home."

"We don't have a previous home," Anna said. "We have lived with David's parents since we got married."

"That's OK," Karen said. "A reference from your manager at work will work too."

"And what about your commission?" David asked. "Who pays it?"

"The owner pays my commission," Karen said. "You don't pay anything to me."

That week, Karen showed them 3 places. The first place was in a great location, but dogs were not allowed. The second place allowed dogs, but it was too far from the train. The third place was the best of all. It was in a good location, dogs were allowed, and the cost was right for their income.

Anna and David sent their income papers and 2 references. 3 days later, the owner said yes. "We are going to have our own home!" Anna said. Max was happy too.

Questions:
Who have Anna and David lived with since they got married?
They have lived with David's parents since they got married.
Why is the location important to Anna and David?
The location is important because they both work in the center of the city and want to be near the train.
What 2 things do most owners ask for?
Most owners ask for papers that show your income and a reference.
Who pays Karen's commission?
The owner pays Karen's commission.
Why was the third place the best?
It was in a good location, dogs were allowed, and the cost was right for their income.

lessons.title: Moving Day
lessons.summary: Emily moves to a third-floor home eight miles away with the help of her brother and a friend.
lessons.text:
Last Saturday was my moving day. My new home is eight miles from my old one, on the third floor of an old building. I didn't want to pay a moving company, so I got a big vehicle for one day from a shop near my house. My brother Sam and my friend Nina came to help me.

We started early, at 7. The vehicle was big, and we needed all of it, because I had nearly 40 boxes. Some boxes were light, but the boxes of books were very heavy. My bed and my table were the heaviest things of all.

Moving everything out of my old place was quick, because it was on the first floor. The drive was quick too: eight miles is not very far. The hard part was the third floor. The building is old, so there is no elevator. We carried every heavy box up to the third floor.

At 12, we were nearly done. We sat on the floor of my new living room and had a quick meal. "Emily, how many books do you have?" Sam asked. "Too many!" I said.

At 2, Sam took the vehicle back to the shop. He drove quickly, because there was an extra cost if the vehicle came back after 3. He was at the shop at 2:30, so I didn't have to pay anything extra.

Nina and I started to open the boxes. We worked quickly. By the evening, the floor was completely clean, my bed was ready, and the books were on the floor next to the wall.

My new home was not completely ready, but it was mine. I gave Sam and Nina some extra money for food, and I thanked them many times. I also learned one thing that day: next time, I'm going to have fewer books!

Questions:
How far is Emily's new home from her old one?
Her new home is eight miles from her old one.
Why did Emily need a big vehicle?
She needed a big vehicle because she had nearly 40 boxes.
What were the heaviest things?
The bed and the table were the heaviest things.
Why did Sam drive quickly?
He drove quickly because there was an extra cost if the vehicle came back after 3.
What is Emily going to do next time?
Next time, she is going to have fewer books.

lessons.title: A Letter from Oakton
lessons.summary: In an e-mail to her sister, Jenny describes the small town she has moved to and its nature.
lessons.text:
Hi Kate,

I'm sorry that I haven't written to you for a long time. We have been very busy since we moved to Oakton. I want to tell you about our new town, because I think you will like it when you visit.

Oakton is a small town about 30 miles from the state capital. It is an old town. Farmers established it in 1850, and some of the buildings that they built are still on Main Street. In the town library, there is a small room with old pictures of the farmers who established the town. It is very interesting.

Recently, Oakton has seen a lot of growth. Many families have moved here from the capital, because homes here cost less. People say that the growth is good for the shops. A new school has opened recently too.

But for me, the best thing about Oakton is nature. There is a river and a big park with old trees near our house. Throughout the year, people walk and fish there. Right now it is spring, and nature is beautiful. There are flowers throughout the town, and the sun is warm. On Sunday, I sat by the river in the sun for 2 hours. I didn't do anything. I just sat in the sun and watched the water.

Life here is slower than life in the capital. When I lived in the capital, I never had any peace. There were always cars and people everywhere. Here, I have peace. At night, I only hear the river.

Please come and visit us this spring. I'll show you the old buildings, the library and the river. I'm sure that you will find Oakton as interesting as I do.

Love,
Jenny

Questions:
How far is Oakton from the state capital?
Oakton is about 30 miles from the state capital.
Who established Oakton, and when?
Farmers established Oakton in 1850.
Why have many families moved to Oakton recently?
They have moved to Oakton because homes there cost less than in the capital.
What is the best thing about Oakton for Jenny?
For Jenny, the best thing about Oakton is nature.
What did Jenny do on Sunday?
She sat by the river in the sun for 2 hours.
Why does Jenny have more peace in Oakton?
She has more peace because life there is slower, and at night she only hears the river.

lessons.title: The Old House on Hill Street
lessons.summary: Before she buys a 100-year-old house, Rosa asks a house expert to check it, and they find a solution to its one problem.
lessons.text:
Rosa wanted to purchase her first house. She looked at many houses, but most of them cost too much. Then she found an old house on Hill Street. The house was 100 years old, and the price was low.

The house was not perfect. The paint was old, and the garden in front of the house was a mess. But Rosa loved it. It was big, with 1,800 square feet and 3 bedrooms. The garden was big too: it was 50 feet long. "This house has a lot of potential," she thought.

Before the purchase, Rosa wanted to avoid any big problems. So she asked a man named Mr. Hall to check the house. It is his job to check old houses before people buy them.

Mr. Hall spent 3 hours in the house. First, he checked the structure. "The structure is very good," he said. "The walls are strong, and the floors are strong too. They built houses well 100 years ago."

Then he found a small problem in the wall by the back door. It was a hole about 1 foot wide. "This hole is only 1 foot wide, so it's easy to fix," Mr. Hall said.

Rosa laughed when he showed her a light switch in the living room. When you used the switch, nothing happened. "I don't know its function," Mr. Hall said. "In old houses, some things have no function anymore."

At the end, Mr. Hall told her his only real concern. "My concern is the heat," he said. "The windows are very old, so the house loses a lot of heat in winter. You will pay big bills for heat."

"Is there a solution?" Rosa asked.

"Yes, the solution is simple," he said. "New windows. They cost money, but they will help you avoid big bills for many years."

Rosa thought about it for a day. The structure was good, the hole was only 1 foot wide, and there was a solution for the heat. She made the purchase the next week. Now she lives in the old house on Hill Street, and she has new windows.

Questions:
Why did Rosa like the old house?
She liked it because it was big and had a lot of potential.
What did Mr. Hall check first?
He checked the structure first.
How wide was the hole in the wall?
The hole was about 1 foot wide.
What was Mr. Hall's only real concern?
His only real concern was the heat.
What was the solution?
The solution was new windows.

lessons.title: Leo's First Week
lessons.summary: In her diary, a mother writes about her son's hard first week in a new town and how a boy next door helps.
lessons.text:
Monday

We moved into our new house 3 days ago. Today was not easy. My son Leo, who is 7, was crying when I went into his room this morning. He misses his old friends. "I want to go home," he said. I told him that this is our home now, but he started to cry again. I tried to stay positive. "It's normal to miss your friends," I said. "It's normal to cry. But you will make new friends here." I hope that I am right.

Wednesday

This afternoon, I was cleaning the windows when I heard the doorbell ring. A woman and her son were at the door. They live next door. The boy's name is Ben, and he is 8. "Can Leo play?" he asked. At first, Leo was hiding behind me. Then Ben showed him a ball. A few minutes later, the boys were outside, and they were kicking the ball in front of the house. They kicked the ball for 2 hours.

Friday

Ben rang our doorbell again today, and the boys played outside all afternoon. Leo has a secret now. Tonight he told me the secret, because he can't keep secrets from me. He and Ben have a secret place where they hide. It is behind the big tree at the end of the street. "Don't tell anyone, Mom. It's a secret," he said. I can't imagine a happier boy. On Monday he was crying, and today he was laughing all day.

Saturday

Today I went to the store, and a woman said hello to me. At first, I didn't recognize her, because we met only once, for a minute, at my door. Then I recognized her smile. She was Ben's mother. We talked for 20 minutes. Our life is starting to feel normal, and Leo is much more positive now. A week ago, I couldn't imagine life in this town. Now I can. Moving here was definitely the right choice, and Leo definitely thinks so too.

Questions:
Why was Leo crying on Monday?
He was crying because he misses his old friends.
What was his mother doing when the doorbell rang?
She was cleaning the windows when the doorbell rang.
What did Leo and Ben do outside?
They kicked a ball in front of the house for 2 hours.
What is Leo's secret?
He and Ben have a secret place behind the big tree at the end of the street.
Why didn't Leo's mother recognize Ben's mother at first?
She didn't recognize her because they met only once, for a minute, at the door.

lessons.title: The Garage Sale
lessons.summary: Before moving to a smaller home, Linda sells her old things at a garage sale.
lessons.text:
Linda has lived in the same house for 40 years. Now her children are adults, and the house is too big for her. Next month, she is going to move to a smaller home near her daughter. But first, she has to do something with all her old things.

"Have a sale," her daughter said. In Linda's town, garage sales are very popular. On Saturday mornings, there are sales on nearly every street. So Linda decided to have a garage sale too.

She spent a whole week getting ready. She put a price on every item. Most items were cheap. Books were 1 dollar each. Cups were 50 cents. A small table was 10 dollars. The most interesting item was an old radio. It was a very good brand, and Linda put a price of 30 dollars on it.

The biggest item was her collection of old records. Over the years, Linda bought nearly a thousand records. The collection was in 12 boxes. Linda hoped to sell the whole collection for 300 dollars.

On the day of the sale, the first customer came at 7. More customers came every minute. A young man picked up the radio. "I know this brand," he said. "They don't make radios like this anymore." He paid 30 dollars for it and smiled.

At 10, a man looked at the record collection for a long time. "I have a collection too," he said. "But mine is smaller. I'll take all of them." He paid 300 dollars.

Many customers spent more than 20 dollars. One woman spent 60 dollars on books and cups.

At the end of the day, Linda counted the money. She sold more than 200 items and made nearly a thousand dollars. She spent some of it on a nice dinner with her daughter. "That was my first garage sale," Linda said, "and my last!"

Questions:
Why is Linda moving?
She is moving because her children are adults and the house is too big for her.
How much was each book at the sale?
Each book was 1 dollar.
Why did the young man buy the radio?
He bought it because it was a very good brand and they don't make radios like that anymore.
How many records were in the collection?
There were nearly a thousand records in the collection.
How much did Linda make at the sale?
She made nearly a thousand dollars.

lessons.title: Joe and the Window Screen
lessons.summary: Sara sends a request to fix a window screen, and the man who comes teaches her how to do it herself.
lessons.text:
Sara has lived in her new place for 2 months. She likes it a lot, but last week she found a problem. There was a big hole in the screen of her bedroom window. At night, the air was nice, but small flying insects came in through the screen.

Sara didn't know how to fix a screen, so she sent a request to the company that owns the building. She sent the request via the company's app. In the app, she wrote: "There is a hole in my window screen. Can someone fix it?" She also sent a picture of the hole via the app.

The next day, an employee of the company came. His name was Joe, and he has worked for the company for 12 years. Joe is the employee who fixes most things in the building.

"I can fix this screen in 10 minutes," Joe said. "But it's an easy skill. Do you want me to teach you? Then next time, you won't need to send a request."

"Yes, please teach me," Sara said.

Joe showed her how to take the screen out of the window. Then he gave her the new screen material. "Go ahead," he said. "You do it." Sara was not sure about her ability, but she went ahead. She cut the material and put it in. It took her 30 minutes, not 10, but the screen was perfect.

"You have the ability to fix many small things," Joe said. "You just need to learn the skills." He told her about a video channel on the internet. "This channel teaches simple skills for the home," he said. "It is a great resource. I learned many of my skills from a resource like that."

That evening, Sara watched 5 videos on the channel. Now, when something small breaks, she doesn't send a request. She uses her new skills.

Questions:
What problem did Sara find?
She found a big hole in the screen of her bedroom window.
How did Sara send her request?
She sent her request via the company's app.
Who is Joe?
Joe is the employee who fixes most things in the building.
What did Joe teach Sara?
He taught her how to fix the screen.
What resource did Joe tell her about?
He told her about a video channel that teaches simple skills for the home.

lessons.title: The Street Fair
lessons.summary: Nora, who moved to Maple Street recently, meets the people on her street at their annual fair.
lessons.text:
Nora moved to Maple Street in August. She was busy with her new job, so she didn't know the people on her street. Then Mr. Brown, the old man who lives next door, told her about the annual fair. "Every September, the people on Maple Street have an annual street fair," he said. "You will certainly meet everyone there."

The fair was on a Saturday. Everyone on the street came, except one family who was on a trip. The street was closed to cars. There were 2 separate tables: one for the kids and one for the adults. The kids played games at their table, and the adults sat at the separate table and talked.

The adults discussed many things about the street. First, they discussed crime. "There is very little crime on Maple Street," Mr. Brown told Nora. "The last crime occurred 4 years ago. Someone took a bike from a garage. Nothing like that has occurred since then."

Then they discussed the trees. The old trees on Maple Street have a disease. The disease is killing some of them. "The city is going to cut down the trees that have the disease," a woman said. "Next spring, it will plant new trees."

Nora sat next to a woman named Helen. Helen has worked for the Department of Justice in the state capital for 20 years. "Justice is very important to me," Helen said. "I have cared about justice since I was young." Nora found her very interesting.

At the end of the fair, everyone ate together, adults and kids. Nora talked with nearly everyone, except the family who was on the trip. "This was certainly a great idea," she told Mr. Brown. "Now I know my street."

Questions:
When is the annual fair on Maple Street?
The annual fair is every September.
Who didn't come to the fair?
Everyone came except one family who was on a trip.
When did the last crime occur?
The last crime occurred 4 years ago.
What is wrong with the trees?
The old trees have a disease.
Where has Helen worked for 20 years?
Helen has worked for the Department of Justice in the state capital.

lessons.title: A German in Chicago
lessons.summary: Klaus moves from Germany to Chicago for a job, stays in a hotel and finds a home of his own.
lessons.text:
Klaus is German. He is an engineer, and last year a company in Chicago gave him a job. So he moved from Germany to the United States.

The plane trip from Berlin to Chicago took 10 hours. Klaus didn't sleep on the plane. He was too excited. He looked out of the window of the plane and thought about his new life.

For the first 2 weeks, the company paid for a hotel. It was a grand old hotel in the center of the city, with a grand hall and very high windows. Klaus liked the hotel, but he didn't want to live in a hotel for a long time. He wanted a real home.

Every day after work, Klaus looked at places to live. Chicago is a very big city, and he often didn't know which direction to go. He asked people for directions many times. Everyone was very kind and gave him clear directions.

Klaus spoke English well, but speaking English all day was hard work for his brain. "My brain is full," he wrote to his mother in Germany. "Every day my brain learns 50 new words."

There was another problem at the hotel. The man in the next room watched TV every night at a very high volume. Klaus asked him to turn down the volume, but the next night the volume was high again. "I need my own place soon," Klaus thought.

In the second week, he found a small apartment on the north side of the city. On the first floor of his building, there was a German bakery. Klaus didn't know that a German bakery existed in Chicago. Now he buys German bread there every morning.

"I didn't know places like this existed here," he told the woman at the bakery. "Now I feel at home."

Questions:
How long did the plane trip take?
The plane trip took 10 hours.
Where did Klaus stay for the first 2 weeks?
He stayed in a grand old hotel in the center of the city.
Why did Klaus ask people for directions?
He asked for directions because he often didn't know which direction to go.
What was the problem at the hotel?
The man in the next room watched TV at a very high volume every night.
What is on the first floor of his new building?
There is a German bakery on the first floor.

lessons.title: Our First Winter
lessons.summary: A family who moved from Texas to Minnesota gets through an extreme winter with help from a city grant.
lessons.text:
My family moved from Texas to Minnesota last summer. In Texas, winter is short, and it is not very cold. In Minnesota, winter is long, and it can be extreme. Our first winter here was the coldest winter of our lives.

In January, the weather was extreme. For a whole week, it was 20 degrees below zero. There was ice on the roads, ice on the cars and even ice on the inside of our windows. My husband fell on the ice in front of our house, but he was OK.

Our house is old, and it was losing a lot of heat. We had the heat on all day and all night, but the house was still cold. When the gas bill came, it was 400 dollars. "We can't pay this every month," my husband said.

Then a woman who lives next door told us about the city's housing authority. "The housing authority has a program for old houses," she said. "It gives a grant to families who want to make their homes warmer." We called the authority the next day. They sent a man to look at our house, and 2 weeks later, we got a grant of 3,000 dollars. With the grant, we put new windows in the whole house.

The new windows had a big impact. The house was much warmer, and our next gas bill was only 200 dollars. The impact on our family was big too. We were happier, and the kids were not cold at night.

Despite the extreme weather, we started to like winter. Despite the cold, we went outside every day. The kids played outside in the snow, and they liked to catch snow in their hands. "Put on your hat, or you'll catch a cold!" I told them every morning.

Now it is spring, and the ice is gone. Despite everything, we are glad that we moved here.

Questions:
Where did the family move from?
They moved from Texas.
How cold was it in January?
For a whole week, it was 20 degrees below zero.
Why was the house cold?
It was cold because the old house was losing a lot of heat.
What did the family do with the grant?
They put new windows in the whole house.
What impact did the new windows have?
The house was much warmer, and the next gas bill was only 200 dollars.
